I will still do wheat-maize on all 4.1 mu, same as last year. On my land, the safe thing is not to change too much. I only have 4.1 mu, so every bag of fertilizer costs real money, but if I cut too much and the yield drops, that hurts more. I have well irrigation, so I will lean on water and fertilizer to hold yield steady. For wheat, I will use an improved variety like most people around me, put the base fertilizer down before sowing, and then topdress nitrogen around jointing. Wheat on our side needs enough bottom fertilizer and 2 to 3 waterings if I want a decent head and grain fill. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, because the hybrids around here usually stand better and give more grain. After wheat harvest I will go in quickly, mostly simple land prep, keep fertilizer a little heavier on nitrogen, and give water at the key stages if the rain is short. I do not like gambling with low fertilizer rates. I will keep the rates close to what has worked before, with a small push where I think the crop can pay back. I will also keep 2 sprays on each crop in mind, more for control than waiting until the problem gets big.
